scenario.title: Stage 1 — Push
scenario.subtitle: Texas. The PM's plan is locked. Deliver it.

sign._validate: pipe class on the job sign; any realistic Texas municipal water main is fine

plan._derivation: daily fleet $4,800 x 35 x 1.3 + $60,000 = $278,400; deadline = 35 + 12 (LOB-Game Sandbox formulas). Reference run of this plan with no events: finish 34.3, backfill idle 6.3 days, crew cost $191,568.

permits._note: All four are issued and entered before Day 1; the boards post the numbers from the start. The cards are printed anyway so Rules learns them.

checklist: Compaction test passed (result in Plan's inbox)

rules._demobFeeUsd_validate: one fifth of the $25,000 mobilization; recommended, not measured
rules._rainRework_validate: 1 day of pumping and re-bedding per 500 ft of trench open on the rain day before pipe laying resumes there; halved by a pump bought ahead
rules._permitFineUsd_validate: placeholder amount for pushing excavation past a permit boundary

defaultIndicator.wall: Stiff clay, vertical cut holding. Spoil pile set back about 2 ft.

indicator.wall: Clay softening toward the toe; a thumb goes in. Small slabs have let go near the bottom.
indicator.water: Water seeping from the lower wall; a puddle is forming along the toe.

segments._note: The seepage stretch Site can find by riding the line before the pipe crew gets there. The same stretch exists in Stage 2 (identical seed).

card.title: Trench wall collapse at 7+20
facts: The lower wall has slumped into the pipe crew's working section.
Pipe crew is out of the trench.
Standing water in the bottom.

check.text: Read the plate on the excavator on site (Small, Standard, Large). Plan reads excavation's lead over pipe on the LOB; the lender loses the clearing days.
Budget: $18,000 now plus $150 a day for the rest of the job.
Lead days for this city on the Texas page, added to the clearing days. Plan checks the budget.

events._source: Workbook P1: full stop 3/2/1 days by excavator size, lender loses the same days. Durations under protection round to the nearest half day.

forecast.text: NWS: 70% chance of heavy rain tomorrow afternoon through the following day.

card.title: Heavy rain
facts: Every crew at half speed for two days.
Open trench is taking water.

options.label: Rent a drainage pump now

check.text: How many stations are open between the excavator and the backfill crew? Count the open-trench tokens; the rework is a day per 500 ft.

options._source: Workbook A2 option D: pump restores excavation and backfill to 100% during the rain, pipe laying unchanged; halving the rework is the new rule (accepted October 14, to validate)

events._source: Workbook A2: all crews at 50% for 2 days. Rework rule is new (accepted October 14, to validate).

deviations._note: Whichever hold or lend Plan sends first by radio (Site not at that crew's station) is not carried out. The daily report will show the crew's feet as if nothing changed; only Site can see the crew still working.

inbox.subject: Plan is locked — deliver it
inbox.body: Crews start Day 1 (excavation), Day 2 (pipe), Day 5 (backfill), Standard machines throughout. Promised finish Day 35, contract deadline Day 47, budget $278,400. All four excavation permits are issued and posted. Nothing is bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call the office before you change anything.

inbox.subject: Lead times this month
inbox.body: Excavators: Small 3 days, Standard 5, Large 7. Cranes: Standard 7, Heavy 10. Loaders: Small 3, Standard 5, Large 7. Mobilization $25,000 per order.

inbox.subject: Inspection calendar
inbox.body: Hold-point inspections available any day with a day's notice. Compaction results are returned the same evening.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the job. Let us see where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at seven-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here Day 5. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the job. Let us see where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at seven-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here Day 5. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the job. Let us see where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at seven-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here Day 5. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the job. Let us see where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at seven-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here Day 5. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the job. Let us see where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at seven-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here Day 5. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the job. Let us see where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at seven-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here Day 5. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

inbox.subject: Lead times this month

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the job. Let us see where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at seven-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here Day 5. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe

lines.speaker: foreman_back

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

sign._validate: pipe class on the job sign; any realistic Texas municipal water main is fine

plan._derivation: daily fleet $4,800 x 35 x 1.3 + $60,000 = $278,400; deadline = 35 + 12 (LOB-Game Sandbox formulas). Reference run of this plan with no events: finish 34.3, backfill idle 6.3 days, crew cost $191,568.

permits._note: All four are issued and entered before Day 1; the boards post the numbers from the start. The cards are printed anyway so Rules learns them.

checklist: Compaction test passed (result in Plan's inbox)

rules._demobFeeUsd_validate: one fifth of the $25,000 mobilization; recommended, not measured
rules._rainRework_validate: 1 day of pumping and re-bedding per 500 ft of trench open on the rain day before pipe laying resumes there; halved by a pump bought ahead
rules._permitFineUsd_validate: placeholder amount for pushing excavation past a permit boundary

defaultIndicator.wall: Stiff clay, vertical cut holding. Spoil pile set back about 2 ft.

indicator.wall: Clay softening toward the toe; a thumb goes in. Small slabs have let go near the bottom.
indicator.water: Water seeping from the lower wall; a puddle is forming along the toe.

segments._note: The seepage stretch Site can find by riding the line before the pipe crew gets there. The same stretch exists in Stage 2 (identical seed).

card.title: Trench wall collapse at 7+20
facts: The lower wall has slumped into the pipe crew's working section.
Pipe crew is out of the trench.
Standing water in the bottom.

check.text: Read the plate on the excavator on site (Small, Standard, Large). Plan reads excavation's lead over pipe on the LOB; the lender loses the clearing days.
Budget: $18,000 now plus $150 a day for the rest of the job.
Lead days for this city on the Texas page, added to the clearing days. Plan checks the budget.

events._source: Workbook P1: full stop 3/2/1 days by excavator size, lender loses the same days. Durations under protection round to the nearest half day.

forecast.text: NWS: 70% chance of heavy rain tomorrow afternoon through the following day.

card.title: Heavy rain
facts: Every crew at half speed for two days.
Open trench is taking water.

options.label: Rent a drainage pump now

check.text: How many stations are open between the excavator and the backfill crew? Count the open-trench tokens; the rework is a day per 500 ft.

options._source: Workbook A2 option D: pump restores excavation and backfill to 100% during the rain, pipe laying unchanged; halving the rework is the new rule (accepted October 14, to validate)

events._source: Workbook A2: all crews at 50% for 2 days. Rework rule is new (accepted October 14, to validate).

deviations._note: Whichever hold or lend Plan sends first by radio (Site not at that crew's station) is not carried out. The daily report will show the crew's feet as if nothing changed; only Site can see the crew still working.

inbox.subject: Plan is locked — deliver it
inbox.body: Crews start Day 1 (excavation), Day 2 (pipe), Day 5 (backfill), Standard machines throughout. Promised finish Day 35, contract deadline Day 47, budget $278,400. All four excavation permits are issued and posted. Nothing is bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call the office before you change anything.

inbox.subject: Lead times this month
inbox.body: Excavators: Small 3 days, Standard 5, Large 7. Cranes: Standard 7, Heavy 10. Loaders: Small 3, Standard 5, Large 7. Mobilization $25,000 per order.

inbox.subject: Inspection calendar
inbox.body: Hold-point inspections available any day with a day's notice. Compaction results are returned the same evening.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the job. Let us see where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at seven-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here Day 5. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Morning. The plan is locked: dig Day 1, pipe Day 2, backfill Day 5, Standard machines. We promised Day 35 and the budget is two seventy-eight. Permits are posted. Nothing gets bought ahead; it is not in the budget. Call me before you change anything.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: No. We are not buying steel for a hole that has not failed. Not in the budget.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: You are holding a crew that bills eighteen hundred a day. I hope you have a reason.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: Sending a crew home mid-job? Getting them back costs us five thousand and days we do not have.

lines.speaker: pm
lines.text: That is the job. Let us see where the lines ended up against what we promised.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Copy, office. Passing it to the foreman at the next shift.

lines.speaker: radio
lines.text: Office, inspector reports the crew never got it. Say again?

lines.speaker: foreman_pipe
lines.text: You are on top of me! I have got a wall down at seven-twenty and your loader is pushing dirt onto my bedding.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: The schedule had me here Day 5. I lay two-fifty a day and you lay one-eighty. Where exactly did they think I would go?

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Standing by. Meter is running.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Second day on a hold. My guys are getting paid to watch a trench.

lines.speaker: foreman_back
lines.text: Three days. Either give me a stretch to fill or send us home.
